e2: Wer hat heute Zeit, mir beim Umzug zu helfen?
e2t: Who has time to help me move today?
g: Wer asks for a subject and takes a singular verb. Wen asks for an accusative object and wem for a dative object.

e2t: What are you doing on the weekend?
g: Was can be subject or object. With a preposition use forms like womit or worüber.

e2: Wo ist hier die nächste Bushaltestelle?
e2t: Where is the nearest bus stop?
g: Wo asks about a location. Two-way prepositions then take the dative: im Park.

e2: Wohin fahrt ihr dieses Jahr in den Urlaub?
e2t: Where are you going on vacation this year?
g: Wohin asks about a destination: in den Park. Also common: Wo gehst du hin?
Woher asks about an origin. Aus takes the dative: Ich komme aus der Türkei.

e2t: When does the German course start?
g: The question word comes first and the verb second. Separable prefixes go last: Wann fängt … an?

e2: Warum bist du gestern nicht gekommen? – Weil ich krank war.
e2t: Why didn’t you come yesterday? – Because I was sick.
g: Answer with weil and a verb at the end. Wieso and weshalb can also mean why.

e2: Wie komme ich am besten zum Rathaus?
e2t: What is the best way to get to City Hall?
g: Combine wie with adjectives: wie alt, wie lange, wie weit, wie groß.

e2: Wie viele Leute kommen zu deiner Party?
e2t: How many people come to your party?
g: Use wie viel with mass nouns and wie viele with countable plurals: Wie viele Kinder?

e1t: Which bus goes to the center?
e2: Welches Kleid gefällt dir besser, das rote oder das blaue?
e2t: Which dress do you like better, the red or the blue?
g: Decline it like a definite article: welcher, welche, welches. Masculine accusative: welchen.

e2: Wen hast du gestern auf der Party getroffen?
e2t: Who did you meet at the party yesterday?
g: The accusative of wer. Use it with besuchen, sehen, fragen or treffen.

e1t: How long does the film last?
e2t: How long are you staying here?

e1t: How many children do you have?
e2t: How many books do you need?
